title: Redwood + AuroraCloud marketplace integration tech sync
summary: Technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for deep integration, and joint solution deliverables. Discussed Terraform modules, auth and onboarding flows, compliance artifacts (SOC2/KMS), and benchmarks for inference latency. Agreed on next steps for draft listing and POC scope.
topics: security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
action_items: Lena Park - Share draft marketplace listing YAML + asset checklist by 2026-07-15
Marco Diaz - Prepare reference architecture diagram (VPC flow, private control plane) and Terraform snippet by 2026-07-16
Tom Reynolds - Provide AuroraCloud marketplace contract template and asset requirements by 2026-07-13
Priya Singh - Run quick latency baseline on Aurora dev env and share raw CSV by 2026-07-14
next_steps: Redwood to send draft listing + RA diagram (Lena/Marco)
Schedule POC kick-off for week of 2026-07-20
Set up shared Slack channel and repo for assets and Terraform modules
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park, Marco Diaz, Priya Singh (Redwood) / Tom Reynolds, Sara Li, Devon Moore (AuroraCloud)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick call to align on the marketplace integration and the reference arch work we promised. um we'll try to keep it to 45 minutes.
[00:12] Tom Reynolds: yeah thanks Lena. excited to get this moving. Sara and Devon are on deck for the marketplace requirements and the platform side.
[00:18] Sara Li: hi all, our main ask is a clean listing that follows Aurora's asset checklist, and a reference arch that shows network flow for private deployments. also timeline wise market ops wants a draft by next week if possible.
[00:32] Marco Diaz: ok got it. on Redwood side we'll prepare a RA that covers hosted + dedicated + private (VPC). we'll include the control plane interactions, optional on-prem package, and key mgmt notes.
[00:45] Devon Moore: quick question — for private deployments, does Redwood's control plane need inbound access from Aurora, or is that all handled outbound from the customer VPC?
[00:56] Priya Singh: good question. The typical pattern is outbound-only from the customer's VPC to the Redwood private control plane, but we also document an air-gapped on-prem variant. we'll show both in the RA. sometimes the transcripter writes control plane as "control plain" so excuse any typos in the notes.
[01:12] Tom Reynolds: oh nice. for the marketplace listing we need the provisioning flow — how customers install, assign billing, and any marketplace-provided billing hooks. can you map that?
[01:24] Lena Park: yes absolutely. we'll add a provisioning flow: 1) subscribe in Aurora marketplace, 2) send provisioning webhook to Redwood, 3) create customer org and allocatededicated capacity or generate API creds for hosted, 4) optional VPC onboarding steps.
[01:45] Sara Li: webhook schemas are important — we have a sample payload we can share. also billing hooks need a product SKU.
[01:53] Marco Diaz: we'll provide a sample Terraform module for provisioning and for the VPC peering / endpoints. note: we often recommend customers use our customer-managed KMS for keys; we'll call that out.
[02:08] Devon Moore: KMS — do you support HSM-backed keys or is that on roadmap?
[02:15] Priya Singh: we integrate with common KMS providers, and HSM-backed keys via customer KMS/HSM connectors are available in Private. i'll add a note to the RA.
[02:27] Lena Park: can we talk compliance? Aurora legal needs SOC2 and audit logs and retention windows documented.
[02:35] Tom Reynolds: yes SOC2 and data residency — some customers require EU-only storage.
[02:41] Marco Diaz: we'll include a compliance appendix: SOC2 status, encryption in transit and at rest, audit log retention options, SAML/SSO support and RBAC. For EU residency, we show region pinning and private deployment paths.
[02:58] Sara Li: for listing assets we also need a short description, long description, screenshots, and a sample integration guide — prefer markdown.
[03:08] Lena Park: ok we'll assemble that. does Aurora have a preferred file size for screenshots?
[03:12] Sara Li: small web-optimised PNGs are fine. 1200x600 recommended.
[03:18] Tom Reynolds: on the technical side we want to validate latency claims. can you share expected p99 latency for the common models when served via marketplace (hosted) vs dedicated?
[03:29] Marco Diaz: yes — we'll provide a table with p50/p95/p99 for hosted (multi-tenant) and dedicated reserved GPU pool. caveat: p99 depends heavily on sequence length and batch window; we'll include test config.
[03:40] Devon Moore: can you run a quick baseline on our dev region? we can spin up a test project if you give us the steps.
[03:47] Priya Singh: sure, i can run that. Marco and I will put together a benchmark runbook. we'll need an API key and a small dataset and sequence profiles.
[03:57] Tom Reynolds: timeline wise, market ops wants the listing draft by 07-15 and legal wants contract terms by 07-20. does that align?
[04:06] Lena Park: yes, we'll target 07-15 for listing draft. Marco will own the RA diagram and TF snippet by 07-16.
[04:12] Sara Li: perfect. about the POC scope — we want to validate provisioning + auth + latency under a small load and then push to a canary customer.
[04:22] Marco Diaz: for auth, we support SAML SSO for SSO and API key/OAuth for service-to-service. marketplace provisioning will create a customer org and can auto-provision SSO metadata endpoint or provide manual steps.
[04:35] Devon Moore: slight transcription note, i think she said "SSO for SSO" but you meant SAML for SSO.
[04:40] Priya Singh: yeah, that is my bad — SAML SSO.
[04:44] Lena Park: any blocker on the legal side or payment integration?
[04:48] Tom Reynolds: we have standard marketplace terms, but the legal team may want to add clauses for data processing addendum for EU customers. i'll share the template.
[04:56] Marco Diaz: also, one technical constraint — when customers use VPC-private we need to document network egress requirements. some customers do not want any egress to Redwood-managed services; we'll include an on-prem airgapped option though that requires extra support.
[05:12] Sara Li: ok good to know. list that as a limitation in the RA.
[05:18] Lena Park: any competitors we should be aware of that Aurora sees in listings?
[05:21] Tom Reynolds: CloudMart and NovaEdge are on the shortlist — buyers often compare latency/cost and marketplace support.
[05:29] Marco Diaz: noted. we'll include a short competitive positioning blurb.
[05:33] Priya Singh: on deployment automation, we recommend our Terraform module that can create orgs, roles, policies and optionally call out to Aurora's marketplace provisioning webhook. we'll put an example in the repo.
[05:47] Devon Moore: can you show a minimal example during the POC kick-off?
[05:50] Marco Diaz: yeah we can demo a minimal terraform run and show the API calls.
[05:54] Lena Park: ok let's capture decisions: Redwood will produce listing draft + assets, reference arch with VPC and on-prem flows, TF snippets, benchmark runbook and a quick baseline. Aurora will share marketplace webhook schema, contract template, and dev access for baseline.
[06:12] Tom Reynolds: sounds good. any follow-ups about billing integration?
[06:16] Sara Li: we'll need SKU mapping and whether Redwood supports metered usage hooks — do you support metered billing callbacks?
[06:24] Marco Diaz: yes we support metered billing callbacks and can emit usage reports; we'll note expected payload and frequency.
[06:33] Lena Park: great. wrapping up — next steps and owners are in the action items. we'll set up the shared repo and slack. last Q: any red flags?
[06:41] Devon Moore: maybe timing if legal needs extended review, but that's on our side.
[06:45] Lena Park: ok thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the draft assets by 07-15.
[06:50] Speaker 1: thanks all, bye.

(Transcript contains occasional transcription errors: "orgs" may appear as "oar g s", "KV cache" as "K V cache", and proper nouns like AuroraCloud sometimes as "Aurora Cloud".)

Recap / Decisions:
- Draft marketplace listing and RA diagram to be delivered by Redwood by 2026-07-15/16.
- Terraform module + sample provisioning flow to be published to shared repo.
- POC kickoff target week of 2026-07-20.
- Aurora to provide webhook schema, contract template, and dev credentials.

References / Links shared:
- Aurora marketplace asset checklist (Sara to share)
- Redwood reference arch template (will be attached in follow-up)
- Sandbox instructions and benchmark runbook (Marco/Priya to author)
